localBiteReport: The most recent angler-reported catch from Choctawhatchee Bay (approximately one week ago, around November 19) logged two solid redfish during a half-day bay trip running from the harbor out through East Pass and under the bridge — a productive late-fall pattern consistent with this time of year. With water temps at 69°F, November historically delivers some of the bay's best inshore action: redfish are schooled up on docks, bridges, and grass flat edges, speckled trout are active on the flats and in the bayous on the north and east end of the bay, flounder are in the tail end of their fall run near the pass and Mid-Bay Bridge, and sheepshead are starting to show in numbers around bridge pilings and jetties as water cools. Live shrimp under a popping cork and soft plastics on light jigheads remain the go-to bay presentations.
